title: Heston vs Black–Scholes: Fitting the Volatility Smile
dek: One model prices every strike with the same number. The other doesn't have to.
excerpt: Black-Scholes assumes a single, constant volatility — so it predicts the same implied vol at every strike. The market flatly disagrees: implied vol curves into a smile/skew. The Heston model, by letting volatility itself be random, can bend to fit that curve. This piece pits the two against a real SPX-style implied-vol surface and measures who fits, by how much, and at what cost.
